newsitem.title: EGYPT: Investors on fringes as Cairo bourse slides.
newsitem.headline: Investors on fringes as Cairo bourse slides.

text.p: Popular realty, mills and cement stocks failed to buck the downtrend on the Cairo bourse on Wednesday as investors remained sidelined and turnover ebbed to its lowest level since mid-January.

"The volume is below half of the daily average we were seeing last week," said Ahmed al-Helw, of Intercapital Securities. "There has been no real direction. Retail and small investors are just watching, they are seeing a correction.
"Institutional investors have already hedged their positions," he said. "Our expectation is to see a pick-up sometime next week or the week after."
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its overall index fell 1.6 percent, shedding 6.28 points to 384.12 points on low turnover of 40.26 million pounds ($11.87 million).
The cement stocks scooped up much of the trade, but declined like most other shares.
Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA, with 37,477 shares changing hands, shed 0.45 pounds to close at 79 pounds after trade worth 2.7 million.
More than 37,400 Suez Cement shares were traded worth 2.61 million pounds. It ended 2.71 pounds down at 69.8.
"They (cement firms) have the lowest P/E of the available sectors," said Helw.
Misr Free Shops shares rose 1.99 pounds to close at 46.99, after 26,500 shares changed hands.
Trade in Medinet Nasr Housing and Development shares was worth 5.3 million pounds. They closed down 17 pounds to close at 465.
Millers were mixed. Central and West Delta Flour Mills was active but fell 2.01 to 105.49.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 610.81 from 628.66 points on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 261.2 points from 263.35.
Out of the 82 shares traded, 21 gained, 43 lost and 18 ended the day unchanged.
